newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU sees grain, oilseed output rising to 2005/06.
newsitem.headline: EU sees grain, oilseed output rising to 2005/06.

text.p: European Union grain output is expected, on the basis of unchanged farm policies, to rise to 213.9 million tonnes in 2005/06, from 201.6 million in 1996/97, the European Commission said in a market trends report.
Oilseeds output is forecast growing slightly to 12.8 million tonnes, from 12.2 million, over the same period, according to the report being presented to EU farm ministers.

An advance copy of the report, obtained by Reuters, said the cereals forecast was based on a stable grains area of around 36.3 million hectares and an increase in yields to 5.9 tonnes a hectare in 2005/06, from an average 5.1 tonnes between 1994/95 and 1996/97.
The soft wheat area is expected to steadily increase at the expense of barley, rye and oats, but maize and durum wheat sowings are seen stable.
Total cereals consumption is forecast increasing to 177.9 million tonnes in 2005/06, from 169.6 million in 1996/97.
Exports and imports are assume to be respect annual limits set under the 1994 GATT accord.
The EU cereals market, especially for wheat, is expected to be relatively tight up until 2001/02.
After that a rapid increase in stocks, especially intervention stocks, is forecast as a steady growth in yields takes production well above EU consumption.
The forecast of a growing surplus early next century is expected to reinforce EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler's case for further cereals reforms to control output and costs.
EU oilseeds plantings are expected to remain within the limit set by the EU-U.S. Blair House agreement and remain stable at 5.57 million hectares, the report added.
Oilseeds production is seen increasing slightly due to a modest improvement in yields.
